svg.title: Three preregistered bets, H1, H2 and H3, all not supported. Every confidence interval crosses zero.

section.div: Three bets, written down before looking

div.h3: More aroused than usual → lower posterior alpha
div.p: Alpha, the 8 to 13 Hz rhythm at the back of the head, drops when the cortex gets busier. It did not drop. If anything it rose very slightly, the wrong way.

div.h3: More pleasant than usual → more left frontal activity
div.p: Frontal alpha asymmetry is the classic “approach and positive mood” marker. Its link to how pleasant a song felt sat almost exactly on zero.

div.h3: People differ in how strong these links are
div.p: Maybe the effect runs one way for some and the other way for others? The spread between people came out at essentially zero. What looked like individual differences was noise from only 20 songs each.

svg.aria-label: Estimates with 95 percent confidence intervals. All four intervals cross zero and none reaches the shaded predicted direction strongly.
svg.text: person specific · predicted: left of zero
person specific · predicted: right of zero

section.p: Standardized within person effects with 95% intervals. The shaded side of each row is where the hypothesis predicted the dot would land. Every interval straddles zero, including the person specific tests that used only the personal deviation.
